public_rationale: The firm part holds. OpenAI had a net loss of just over $5 billion in 2024 (audited statements reported by Ars Technica). Anthropic's S-1 shows a 2024 net loss of $8.3 billion, up from $1.5 billion in 2023, and an operating loss of $2.98 billion, up from $551 million. Neither company was profitable. The second part is hedged ('doesn't appear to be helping'), so I test it in his terms: was there visible financial improvement by the time of the post? There was not. Absolute losses at both firms were growing. One fair counterpoint: Anthropic's compute cost per dollar of revenue fell sharply from 2023 to 2024, so its ratios were improving even as total losses grew. That does not overturn an impression-level claim that cheaper inference was not yet showing up in the bottom line.
limitations: The OpenAI figures come from leaked statements that OpenAI has not published, although they were reported as audited and checked by the FT.
The 'doesn't appear to be helping' part was judged on absolute losses, not on a causal analysis.
The data used for grading was published after the post, but it describes 2024.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: None of these generative AI companies are profitable, and despite repeated claims that the cost of inference is coming down, that doesn't appear to be helping them.

statement.excerpt: None of these companies are profitable, and despite repeated claims that "the cost of inference is coming down" (the thing that happens when you prompt the model to do something) it doesn't appear to be helping them.

from_speaker: None of these companies are profitable
despite repeated claims that 'the cost of inference is coming down'
it doesn't appear to be helping them
our_interpretation: 'These companies' means the generative AI model companies the passage discusses, chiefly OpenAI and Anthropic.
'Profitable' is read plainly as having positive net income (or at least positive operating income) for the most recent full year before the post, 2024. That choice of period is mine.

'Doesn't appear to be helping them' is a hedged impression, not a claim of measured cause and effect. I test it in his terms: as of the post, did the companies' bottom lines still look no better, with losses and burn still large and growing in absolute terms? I do not require proof that cheaper inference had no effect at all.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI and Anthropic both reported losses for 2024, and their absolute losses or burn were growing into 2024, so there was no visible financial improvement as of February 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Either company was profitable in 2024, or its losses or burn clearly shrank in 2024 in a way an informed reader would see as falling costs helping it.
